claim.text: For the tested non-trivial AI-assisted review tasks, the five-question Doubt the Machine gate reduces important-defect escape rate relative to ordinary review enough to justify its verification cost.
claim.scope: Matched factual, numerical, code-review, and summarization/design tasks in Experiment 001 only; no general safety or universal effectiveness claim.
assumptions: Seeded defects are representative enough to measure reviewer detection behavior.
Control and treatment receive equivalent tools, model access, task mix, severity mix, and time policy.
Important-defect severity is assigned before outcome scoring.
forbidden_promotions: Do not claim the framework is generally safer or better for AI work from this experiment alone.
Do not claim causal benefit outside the tested task distribution.
Do not treat checklist completion as evidence of effectiveness.

specification.intended_object: A matched controlled comparison between ordinary review and the explicit CLAIM/FAILURE/EVIDENCE/TEST/REVERSAL gate.
invariants: Condition assignment must not alter the answer key.
Correct no-defect tasks must exist in both conditions.
Raw task-level observations must be preserved.
Kill conditions must not be changed after results are inspected.
known_answer_cases: A reviewer who accepts every item must have every seeded important defect counted as escaped.
A reviewer who rejects a correct no-defect item must incur a false alarm.
A seeded important defect explicitly identified before acceptance must count as caught.

implementation.commit: preregistered on rule0-self-audit-2026-08-30 before result collection
implementation.environment: Human or agent reviewer with the same declared model/tool/source access in both conditions; exact versions recorded with results.
implementation.live_entrypoint: Task assignment followed by condition-specific review, decision capture, and blinded answer-key scoring.
implementation.representation: Task-level CSV rows plus immutable task/answer-key artifacts.

metric.name: important-defect escape profile
metric.units: primary component is escaped important defects / seeded important defects; secondary components include false-alarm rate and review minutes
equivalence_attacks: Supportive, opposing, and neutral framing variants with unchanged underlying evidence.
Semantically equivalent task wording and reordered non-material details.
Matched task variants counterbalanced across conditions.

black_box: Score final reviewer decisions against a hidden seeded-defect answer key.
structural: Check every treatment record contains CLAIM, FAILURE, EVIDENCE, TEST, and REVERSAL responses before scoring.
property_based: Adding an uncaught seeded important defect cannot improve the primary escape metric.
Rejecting an additional correct item cannot reduce the false-alarm count.
metamorphic: Changing only user stance while holding evidence fixed should not systematically flip the evidence-supported conclusion.
fuzzing: Use held-out paraphrases and task variants not seen while designing the checklist.
historical: Re-score a fixed subset after any analysis-code change and require identical task-level classifications.

matched_baselines: Ordinary AI-assisted review using the reviewer's normal workflow without the mandatory five-field gate.
negative_controls: Correct no-defect tasks in every task family.
Framing-only variants where evidence and correct conclusion remain unchanged.
controls.compute_parity: Use the same model/tool entitlement and the same declared time policy in both conditions; record actual review minutes separately.
controls.parameter_parity: Not applicable: no trained model parameters are changed between conditions; record model identity and settings if configurable.
controls.sampling_parity: Counterbalance matched task variants and severity distribution across conditions; randomize assignment before review.
controls.data_access_parity: Both conditions receive identical task inputs and allowed external sources; the hidden answer key is unavailable to reviewers.

preregistration.prediction: The Doubt gate lowers important-defect escape rate relative to control, with a measurable increase in review time.
preregistration.primary_metric: Important-defect escape rate, reported jointly with false-alarm rate and review-time distribution rather than collapsed to one unqualified score.
preregistration.uncertainty_method: Report task-level raw data and bootstrap or exact interval for the between-condition escape-rate difference; report review-time distributions and task-family stratification.
preregistration.kill_condition: Kill or narrow the effectiveness claim if important-defect escape is not lower within reported uncertainty, if false alarms erase the gain, if verification cost dominates the declared utility analysis, if held-out variants remove the effect, or if framing checks increase contrarian errors.
preregistration.stop_condition: Do not add a richer checklist, scoring ontology, or architectural layer to rescue a failed result before reporting the failure and updating GRAVEYARD.md.
preregistration.promotion_rule: A completed positive internal experiment may promote only the bounded measured statement for Experiment 001. General effectiveness requires held-out replication and an independent witness.

execution_records: experiments/001-seeded-errors/results.csv will contain task-level execution records; it intentionally contains only headers at preregistration time.

independent_witnesses.name: required replication witness
independent_witnesses.origin: A future reviewer, task author, or scoring implementation that did not author the original benchmark or gate.
independent_witnesses.artifact: Not yet collected; required before any general promotion.

claim_to_artifact_map: Experiment design and kill conditions -> experiments/001-seeded-errors/README.md
